title: Undo a commit everyone already has

terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Run the setup to build the repository, then work inside repo/ with git.

tasks.title: Undo the bad fares without rewriting history
tasks.description:
Run `node setup.mjs`, then work inside `repo/`.

The commit `Load spring fares` on `main` multiplied every price by ten, and it is already shared. Undo it on `main`.

The check reads your repository and expects:

- `fares.txt` on `main` is exactly what it was before `Load spring fares`
- `timetable.txt` on `main` still has the Sunday sailings
- all four original commits, including the bad one, are still in `main`'s history
- no merge, revert or rebase is left half done, and the working tree is clean
nextSteps: Run `node setup.mjs`, then `cd repo` and list the history with `git log --oneline`.
Use `git show` on the suspicious commit to see exactly what it changed.
Undo that one commit with a new commit, without opening an editor.
Run `git log --oneline` and `git status` to confirm the result.
hints: Moving main backwards would remove commits other people already have. Look for a command that adds a commit instead.
`git revert` takes the commit you want to cancel, not the one you want to go back to.
Pass the hash of `Load spring fares` to `git revert` together with `--no-edit`, then check `git status` is clean.

tasks.title: Share the fix
tasks.description:
Push your fixed `main` to the shared remote `origin` (it lives in `.shared.git` next to `repo/`).

The check expects:

- `main` on `origin` has the original fares and the Sunday sailings
- `main` on `origin` still contains all four original commits (the remote refuses forced, non-fast-forward pushes)
- your local `main`, your `origin/main` and `main` on `origin` all point at the same commit
nextSteps: Run `git status` and read how far main is ahead of origin/main.
Run `git log --oneline --decorate -n 3` and check where origin/main points.
hints: If your main only adds commits on top of what origin has, a plain push works.
If the push was rejected as non-fast-forward, your main lost commits that origin has. Run setup again and undo with a new commit.
Run `git push origin main` after the revert. Afterwards `git status` should say your branch is up to date with origin/main.
